overview: In the Signature teaching of military history, What Military History Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. key_laws: Clausewitz's trinity: passion, chance, and reason in war.

Friction: the countless small things making war unpredictable.
methods: Battlefield analysis: terrain, forces, and decisions reconstructed.

title: The Future of Military History — Fundamentals of Military History
description: Signature edition. This entry teaches The Future of Military History as part of the fundamentals of military history, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Advanced tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of military history, The Future of Military History is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Technology means how weapons transform warfare, from stirrups to drones. Intelligence means knowing the enemy, from spies to signals. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Technology: how weapons transform warfare, from stirrups to drones.
Intelligence: knowing the enemy, from spies to signals.
key_laws: Principles of war: mass, economy of force, surprise, and the rest.

methods: Archival research: orders, diaries, and reports as evidence.
history: Military history is ancient, from Thucydides to Vegetius; staff colleges professionalized it in the 19th century. World wars made it central, and it now studies war's full social, technological, and ethical dimensions.
